paths.title: Start with close, consolidation and reconciliation
paths.answer: Compare the financial-close customer panel, short consolidation/reconciliation agent demo and optional continuous-close workshop. Use accounting operations sessions for balances, exceptions, root causes and review.
paths.limit: Do not equate GL operations, EPM consolidation, reconciliation and narrative reporting. No dedicated intercompany/elimination session was verified; ask how those requirements map to the intended products.

paths.title: Connect practical experience with ERP/EPM direction
paths.answer: Use separate ERP and EPM roadmap sessions, then test the direction against Hearst, EPM customers and adoption case studies.
paths.limit: A customer panel can include current use, exploration and plans. A roadmap, demonstration or conference workshop is not a delivery commitment, GA assertion or license entitlement.

paths.title: Keep reporting and variance analysis tied to the required output
paths.answer: Compare EPM narrative/close practice, Ledger variance investigation, Cigna's warehouse-to-Excel approach, Oracle Finance analytics and optional FP&A guidance.
paths.limit: Formatted reporting, commentary, operational reports, dashboards and conversational analysis are different outputs. FDI, OAC, OTBI, BI Publisher and EPM are not interchangeable; no integration or licensing is assumed.

paths.title: Build trusted information and preserve accounting controls
paths.answer: Prioritize enterprise structures, hierarchy stewardship, finance data readiness and controls assurance. Use EDM workshop or testing guidance only if that depth helps her team.
paths.limit: AI does not remove human approvals, professional judgment or audit accountability. Software testing does not itself certify financial statement accuracy or control effectiveness.

paths.title: Ask what improved, how it was adopted and how it was measured
paths.answer: Look for customer evidence on process standardization, preparation effort, exception handling, timeliness, training and user adoption. Compare the operating model as well as the technology.
paths.limit: Suggested measures are discussion prompts, not Atmus metrics. Lexington's published 40% conversion and 85% expense-processing improvements are transformation outcomes, not AI-only or close-duration results. Other numerical ROI is not invented.
